title: Introduce tenant key-usage quotas, RBAC v2 delegation tokens, and adaptive audit-sampling
author: Leah Martinez
description:
Motivation: Several customers and the compliance team requested clearer controls on cryptographic operations (KMS calls) per tenant to cap noisy tenants and provide predictable billing. We also need a safe way to delegate short-lived RBAC v2 privileges to service identities used by 3rd party integrators, and to reduce high-cardinality audit log volume for high-throughput tenants while retaining attestation guarantees.

This PR implements three coordinated features: tenant-scoped key-usage quotas (soft throttles + hard caps), RBAC v2 delegation tokens (auditable, short TTL, scope-limited), and an adaptive audit-sampling pipeline (policy-driven sampling with deterministic attestation tags so sampled events can still be reconstituted for compliance).

What changed (high level):
- pkg/kms/quota: quota engine, tenant counters, integration points with the KMS proxy to enforce soft/hard limits and emit quota metrics. Quotas are configurable per-tenant via the console or infra config; overrides for dedicated/private customers are supported.
- services/rbac/delegation: new delegation token issuer, API surface for requesting delegated scopes, token revocation hooks, and integration with the policy evaluator. Delegation tokens are signed, include a tenant and scope claim, and are enforced by cluster gateways.
- observability/audit-sampler: adaptive sampling controller that runs alongside the audit forwarder. Policies can express deterministic sampling keys (e.g., request_id mod N) and preserve attestation headers so sampled traces are linkable to unsampled aggregates. Includes retention/rehydration markers for on-demand full replays.
- console: admin UI additions to configure tenant KMS quotas and delegation token lifetime.
- tests: unit + e2e tests covering quota enforcement under bursty load, delegation token authorization matrices, and sampling correctness with deterministic keys.

Design notes: quotas use a leaky-bucket approximation with configurable burst allowance and a hard enforcement path that returns a 429-like KMS policy error (mapped to our API error model). Delegation tokens are implemented as signed JWT-like envelopes with a signed key id and revocation list; we introduced a small CRDT-backed revocation cache replicated to gateways for low-latency checks. Audit sampling is pluggable and deterministic: the same request will always be sampled the same way given the policy, which keeps compliance proofs reproducible.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind a console flag + feature toggle. Initial rollout will be opt-in for a set of pilot tenants. We will enable metrics and set alerts on quota rejects, delegation token failures, and audit-sampler coverage drift.

Risk and mitigations:
- False positives on hard quotas: we added a 24-hour grace window and telemetry to quickly revert to soft-only behavior.
- Delegation token leakage: tokens are short-lived (default 5m) and scope-restricted. Revocation path added.
- Sampling losing required evidence: deterministic sampling keys + rehydration markers ensure we can reconstruct sampled events for an incident.

Related work: references SUP-9443 (support ticket), ENG-1218 (quota engine backlog), ENG-1229 (delegation token spec).

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests in perf harness, [x] docs in security/README updated, [x] console feature toggles, [x] release notes
